compatibility.admission_policy: Protocol 1.1 requires its own clean source revision, native plugin digest, protocol-1.1 native receipt, complete A1-A6 live receipt, baseline fortress/citizen evidence re-executed for protocol 1.1, server binary receipt, exact registry entry, trusted monotonic floor, and single-use process admission. It inherits no authority from protocol 1.0.

coverage.announcement_caveat: The bridge exposes a bounded retained suffix after one cursor. A gap before the oldest retained report is explicit. No response proves complete fortress announcement history.

security_invariants: Both methods authenticate before inspecting world, citizen, or report state.
Protocol 1.1 registers no mutation RPC methods.
No RunCommand, RunLua, keyboard, pause, dig, labor, military, teleport, checkpoint, restore, arbitrary forwarding, or client-selected method exists.
The handshake publishes exact protocol, bridge, plugin generation, and two-method manifest identity.
Announcement records are returned inside the same ReadObservation reply as fortress and citizen fields.
Citizen pagination requires paused-world summary and announcement fields to remain identical across pages before one capsule is published.

The Rust client rejects malformed protobuf, duplicate fields, nonminimal varints, noncanonical booleans, invalid UTF-8, generation drift, method-manifest drift, cursor drift, retained-window drift, and noncanonical report order.
Announcement records and text are bounded before canonical publication.
Unknown protobuf fields do not alter semantic identity or grant authority.
A complete retained suffix grants no capability and is not an effect receipt.
